text: Forge Out is a circuit optimizer and equivalence checker for Tape Out circuits on X Layer. You give it a circuit. It returns a smaller or shallower one, and checks that both behave identically on every input.

caption: How it works · three steps
text: It works in three steps. One: optimize. Exact synthesis up to three inputs, and rewriting for larger functions. Two: prove. Every result is checked against the original, exhaustively up to twenty inputs. Three: tape out. You copy the ready-made call data and send it from your own wallet.

caption: Step 1 · optimize, live in the browser
text: Here is step one, live in the browser. Nothing is sent to a server. We paste a Boolean expression, a three input majority, choose the area objective, and press Optimize. The result is six nand gates, checked equivalent by exhaustive truth table comparison, with a netlist you can download.

caption: The same step from the command line
text: The command line tool does the same, and adds A B C for larger circuits. One command takes the expression and prints the gate count, the depth, the estimated gas, and the netlist.

caption: FabX replay · 46 tasks with a complete spec
text: We tested it on Fab X's public task bank. Of the forty six tasks with a complete specification, Forge Out beats the reference on twenty two, ties eleven, and loses thirteen. The largest gap is task G C twelve. Reference cost: four hundred ninety six thousand. Ours: twenty eight thousand, six hundred seventy two.

caption: Step 2 · prove, with a second independent tool
text: Step two matters most. A second tool, written from scratch in Python with no shared code, re-checks every beat. Twenty two tasks. Twenty five thousand, eight hundred fifty six output bits. Zero mismatches.

caption: 22 checked circuits · netlist and calldata to copy
text: Every checked circuit is on the site, with its netlist and its tape out call data, ready to copy.

caption: Step 3 · on chain, read-only check against X Layer
text: Step three is on chain. This command reads a real circuit from X Layer, and compares the processor's answer with our local simulation. They match.

caption: ForgeRegistry v2 · live on X Layer
text: Five showcase circuits are taped out and listed in Forge Registry on X Layer. Four are verified on chain through the processor's own eval. The fifth has eight inputs, so it is attestation only.

caption: What ForgeOut does not claim
text: And the limits are stated plainly. Minimal results are proven only up to three inputs. The reference still wins thirteen tasks. And we make no reward or fabrication claims. Try it at forge out dot x y z.
